description: Shared Windows services contract fixture between fivenines-agent and fivenines-server. Source of truth: fivenines-agent tests/fixtures/windows_services_contract_payload.json, asserted end-to-end by tests/test_windows_services.py::test_contract_fixture_round_trip -- each scenario's 'scm' is served by a fake win32service module (the pywin32 calls the collector makes: OpenSCManager, EnumServicesStatusEx, OpenService, QueryServiceConfig, QueryServiceConfig2) plus the trigger count the agent reads through ctypes, and windows_services() must equal scenario['payload']['windows_services']. 'scm' is an agent-side input the server ignores. The server ingests data['windows_services'] == payload['windows_services']; it is a TOP-LEVEL config flag, config['windows_services'] = true, a plain boolean, sent to Windows agents only. Change the payload shape only in lockstep with the server spec and its byte-identical fixture copy.
_agent_min_version_note: MINOR on the 1.x train: a new collector. Gate the config flag on it (older agents ignore the unknown key, so an ungated flag is harmless, just inert).
null_contract: data['windows_services'] ABSENT means not reported: an older agent, the flag off, or the windows_services capability probed false (pywin32 missing, or the Service Control Manager refused the agent's account; the reason is in capability_reasons). null means the collection failed this tick: not Windows, the Service Control Manager could not be opened or listed, more than 2000 services were listed, or a read blocked past the agent's 10s bound (then null on every tick until that read returns). Neither ABSENT nor null says anything about any service: keep every stored row as it is, open no incident and resolve none.
list_contract: {'services': [...]} is every Win32 service the agent's account can see, sorted by name (case-insensitively), drivers and per-user services excluded (a per-user service template, type bit 0x40, and its per-logon instances, named <template>_<LUID>, which come and go with each logon). It is NOT proof that a missing service was removed: the Service Control Manager silently omits a service whose security descriptor denies the account SERVICE_QUERY_STATUS, and the account is a non-administrator. A service that disappears was uninstalled OR hidden; prune it only after it has been absent for a while (the server's choice), never on one tick. {'services': []} is a real (if unlikely) answer: nothing visible.
entry_contract: Every entry has exactly these keys. name: the service (key) name, unique on the host, case-insensitive in Windows -- the row identity. display_name: as services.msc shows it, in the OS install language. state: 'stopped', 'start_pending', 'stop_pending', 'running', 'continue_pending', 'pause_pending' or 'paused' (null for a value outside them, which Windows does not send). start_type: 'automatic', 'manual' or 'disabled' ('boot' and 'system' exist for drivers only); null when the account may see the service but not read its configuration. delayed_auto_start: bool, the 'Automatic (Delayed Start)' flag (read for every service, meaningful for automatic ones only); null when unreadable. trigger_start: bool, true when the service has start or stop triggers ('(Trigger Start)' in services.msc): such a service starts and stops on its own, so 'automatic and stopped' is not a failure for it; null when unreadable. pid: the service process id, null when it has none (stopped or starting). exit_code: Win32ExitCode as reported, an int: 0 after a clean stop, 1077 for a service never started since boot, 1066 (ERROR_SERVICE_SPECIFIC_ERROR) when the service set its own code, which is then service_exit_code (an int, shipped as reported). The state, start type and flags are read on every tick, uncached.

scenarios.name: typical_server
scenarios.comment: A running automatic service; an automatic service that stopped after a failure (exit 1066 with its own code 3: an incident); a manual trigger-start service never started (1077); an automatic delayed trigger-start service that stopped cleanly on its own (not a failure); a disabled one; a paused one; a localized display name; a service whose configuration the account cannot open (listed, start type unknown); one whose delayed-start and trigger reads both failed (start type known, flags unknown); and, absent from the payload, a per-user service template, its per-logon instance, and a service deleted between the listing and its configuration read.

scenarios.name: nothing_visible
scenarios.comment: The listing succeeded and showed nothing (every service hidden from the account): an empty list, not null.

scenarios.name: scm_refused
scenarios.comment: OpenSCManager refused (error 5): a failed collection, null. The capability probe makes the same open, so a steady refusal makes the key ABSENT instead, with the reason in capability_reasons.

scenarios.name: listing_failed
scenarios.comment: The SCM opened but EnumServicesStatusEx failed: null, never a partial list.
